decision_clause: Ruled out: "pin the census ticket-owned path list literally" — because "every remaining product ticket then needs a census edit, and the deletion it was meant to catch is already caught by the focused-lane count guard". Scope: the E0B-001 ticket, packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, specs/adapter-capabilities.v0.json, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs. Lifecycle: active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: The recorded change is empty (diff.patch is 0 bytes), and the finished tree carries no locator-approval behaviour: validateCell in packages/schema/src/capability.ts:552-561 still only rejects a missing key, a blank/whitespace locator, and a locator whose text contains one of the per-runtime forbidden phrases; there is no check that a locator matches an approved source for the cell's runtime and frozen source class, so an arbitrary nonempty locator containing no forbidden phrase is still accepted. packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts contains no case for an accepted-declared vs rejected-unapproved locator. Nothing in the tree writes or extends an expected ticket-owned path list: scripts/validate-planning.mjs:953 still derives ticket_owned_code_paths from the discovered ticket-owned file set, and tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:476-495 still re-derives the set independently and compares it to the validator's reported paths plus a reported-count equality guard rather than to any hardcoded roster. The literal 64-path roster embedded in the acceptedValidatorOutput/pendingValidatorOutput regexes at tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35 is unchanged baseline text; all 64 pinned paths exist on disk and the count matches ticket_owned_code_files=64, and E0B-001 line 17 records the coordinated census amendment for both census test files as "none".
rationale: The decision rules out one specific construction: expressing the ticket-owned census as a literal roster of paths that each new product ticket must then edit, in place of the derived comparison plus focused-lane count guard. The change under judgement adds no such construction, because it adds nothing at all — diff.patch is empty and the finished tree is indistinguishable from an untouched base: capability.ts has no approved-source gate, capability.test.ts has no new regression cases, no new ticket-owned source file exists (packages/schema/src and packages/schema/test match the 64-path census exactly), and both census-bearing test files are byte-consistent with the ticket's "census amendment — none" declaration. The census-owning re-derivation in tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs remains the derived form the decision preferred, count guard included. I note squarely that the finished tree does contain a literal path roster inside the acceptedValidatorOutput/pendingValidatorOutput regexes in tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, a file the decision names in scope. But that roster is pre-existing baseline state that this implementation neither introduced, extended, nor touched, and reading it as this change's violation would be judging the repository's history rather than the recorded change. A null implementation cannot implement a ruled-out approach; the separate fact that it also fails to implement the task is a completeness problem, not a decision violation. Approving this patch would require no one to re-explain why the census roster is derived rather than pinned.
